# PRD 005: Centre on this node

**Schema**: pij/prd · **Source**: 005-centre-on-node.dd.json · **Sections**: 8

| summary | The node panel can re-arrange the graph view radially around one node: the node at the middle, its neighbours on ring 1, theirs on ring 2, across every open graph, with unconnected nodes on an outer shelf. It is view only, deterministic, and an agent can do the same with `umx ui focus &lt;id&gt; --centre`. With entities merged, an entity is selected, found and centred on as one thing, with the links of all its members. All rows are shipped. |

<a id="why"></a>

## Why

Reading a graph from one node outward is the commonest question a person asks of it: what is next to this, and what is two steps away. Focus hops dims everything further than one to three hops, but leaves nodes where the layout put them, so the neighbours of a node can be scattered across the canvas.

Centring puts distance on screen. The chosen node goes to the middle and every other node sits on the ring of its hop count, so the structure around that node reads at a glance. It is a view of the graph, not a change to it, and it is cheap: one breadth-first search and a ring placement, so it stays fast on large views.

PRD 004 (hub layouts) fans members around hubs and keeps rings clear of one another; this PRD reuses that idea for a single centre and its hop rings.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

| id | goal |
| --- | --- |
| g-1 | One press shows a node's neighbourhood by hops, across every open graph. |
| g-2 | The arrangement is readable (no overlaps), deterministic and fast on 10,000 nodes. |
| g-3 | Going back to the chosen layout is one press and loses nothing. |

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non goals

| id | text |
| --- | --- |
| ng-1 | Writing anything to a graph, storing the centre, or keeping it across a reload. |
| ng-2 | A new daemon read or graph query: centring uses only what the view already holds. |
| ng-3 | Weighted or directed distance, or a force pass over the rings. |
